claims.claim: The Gospels were set out in the church called the Constantinian; the first session is dated III Nones October, eighth indiction, ninth year of Constans
Bishops and priests sat, deacons and clergy stood
claims.witness: mansi_sacrorum-conciliorum-collectio-tomus-10-lat_welter-facsimile1901.txt l.82077-82079 (Book of the Popes, as reprinted in Mansi)

claims.claim: The synod met by the sacred order and canonical care of Martin
Duchesne dates the five sessions to 5, 8, 17, 19 and 31 October 649
The Ekthesis confesses one will of Christ and forbids speaking of one or two operations
Paul of Constantinople's letter to Pope Theodore: one will of Christ
The Typos forbids any dispute about one will or two
Constans was Heraclius's grandson
Martin: Paul persuaded the emperor to issue the Typos to destroy catholic teaching, and overturned the Roman see's altar in the house of Placidia
The Book of the Popes counts 105 bishops
Bede: the synod of the blessed Pope Martin and 105 bishops; John brought its decision to be copied at Wearmouth
The attendance list names 105 bishops and one priest besides Martin; the subscriptions repeat them in order with three later signers
claims.witness: mansi_sacrorum-conciliorum-collectio-tomus-10-lat_welter-facsimile1901.txt l.88794-88949, 114801-115403 (each name-and-see line counted in the Latin column)

claims.claim: Theophanes: 150 bishops (Goar's Latin); 110 (Anastasius's Latin version)
Maurus of Ravenna was represented by Maurus of Cesena and the priest Deusdedit, and wrote that army and people kept him home for fear of raids
Stephen of Dor presented his petition, telling how Sophronius sent him to the apostolic see
Greek abbots and monks asked to enter and Martin admitted them
The synod said the Typos had a good aim but a force at odds with it
Canon 18 anathematizes Theodore of Pharan, Cyrus, Sergius, Pyrrhus and Paul, the Ekthesis and the Typos, and again Severus and Theodosius
Martin asked Amandus to have Sigebert send bishops to carry the acts to the emperor
Duchesne: copies went to the emperor, Philadelphia, Carthage and Maastricht, with an encyclical
Constans, furious, had Martin and Maximus brought to Constantinople, tortured and exiled to Cherson
At Bizya, Theodosius said the Roman synod lacked force, being held without the emperor's order
Hatfield received the synod held in Rome under Martin
Theophanes files the affair under the nineteenth year of Heraclius
Martin died in exile at Cherson
claims.witness: the account by one of his clergy, mansi tomus 10 l.88330-88336

contested_claims.sides: 105: the acts' attendance list and signatures (Mansi l.88794-88949, 114801-115403), the editors' heading (l.88609-88616), the Book of the Popes (l.82051-82052), Bede (l.10403), Binius from the signatures (l.117331-117333). 150: Theophanes in Goar's Latin (l.60749-60750). 110: Anastasius's Latin version of Theophanes (l.116628), which Binius quotes (l.117107).

contested_claims.claim: Whether Maximus the Confessor was present
contested_claims.sides: Theophanes: he came from Africa and fired Martin's zeal (l.60747-60750), not that he sat. Fabricius, modern: he took part (PG 90 l.280-281). A 'Maximus monachus' signs the monks' petition (Mansi l.92672), beside a margin note that the Greek manuscript lacks the signatures (l.92483-92487). Binius: the acts make no mention of Maximus (l.117109-117110).

contested_claims.claim: Whether the synod was held without the emperor's consent
contested_claims.sides: Theodosius at Bizya, hostile, in a record from Maximus's side: held 'injussu imperatoris' (PG 90 l.9579-9582). The acts say Martin called it, and name no imperial order. W. D. Foulke, modern: Martin's appointment lacked the emperor's confirmation (paul-the-deacon_history-of-the-langobards_foulke1907.txt l.9938-9939). Binius, against: Constans first confirmed Martin's election in the usual way, then asked him to approve the Typos (Mansi tomus 10 l.117080-117094).

claims.claim: Easter was once kept twice in one year at Oswy's court; the king had kept the feast while Queen Eanfleda and her followers were still keeping Palm Sunday; the queen followed the custom of Kent, with her priest Romanus
Oswy, taught and baptized by the Scots, 'thought nothing better than what they taught'
Bede finished his History in 731
Stephen was of Wilfrid's household; his Life was written within a few years of Wilfrid's death in 709; he came north with Wilfrid in 669
claims.witness: James Raine, preface (byrhtferth_vita-s-oswaldi-in-historians-of-the-church-of-york-v1-lat_raine1879.txt (Stephen, Life of Wilfrid) l.1676-1684, 1755-1770)

claims.claim: The controversy concerned Easter, the tonsure and other church matters; a synod was agreed at Streaneshalch, where the abbess Hild presided
claims.witness: Bede III.25 (bede_ecclesiastical-history-english-people_giles1903.txt l.7955-7962; Latin, Plummer l.21394-21396)

claims.claim: The kings, father and son, came; Colman with his Irish clergy; Agilbert with the priests Agatho and Wilfrid; James and Romanus on their side; Hild and her followers for the Scots, as was Cedd, interpreter for both parties
Stephen names Hild as present, the two kings, the bishops Colman and Agilbert, and the priests Agatho and Wilfrid
Agilbert was bishop of the West Saxons and by nation a Frank, who had lived long in Ireland
Oswy opened: those who served one God should observe the same rule of life
Colman: he kept the Easter received from the elders who sent him as bishop, the Easter of John the Evangelist
claims.witness: Bede III.25 (bede_ecclesiastical-history-english-people_giles1903.txt l.7984-7993); Stephen 10 (byrhtferth_vita-s-oswaldi-in-historians-of-the-church-of-york-v1-lat_raine1879.txt (Stephen, Life of Wilfrid) l.5128-5136)

claims.claim: Agilbert asked that Wilfrid speak in his stead, since he could explain it better in English than Agilbert by an interpreter
Wilfrid spoke for the Easter kept at Rome, where Peter and Paul were buried, and called the Picts and the Britons the accomplices in obstinacy of the Irish party (polemic)
The exchange on the keys: 'It is true, O king!' ... 'None.'; Peter 'is the door-keeper, whom I will not contradict'; all present gave their assent
Oswy, smiling, asked the whole synod whether Columba or Peter was greater in heaven, and the synod answered with one voice; the king then ruled for Peter
Bede dates the disputation to 664, the twenty-second year of Oswy and the thirtieth of the Irish bishops among the English
Agilbert went home; Colman took those who would not accept the Catholic Easter and the tonsure and went back to consult his people; Cedd accepted the Catholic Easter
Eata was made abbot of Lindisfarne at Colman's request, for the king much loved Colman; Colman took part of Aidan's bones
Colman went with the Irish of Lindisfarne and about thirty English to Iona, then Inishbofin, then founded Mayo for the English
Wilfrid was chosen bishop and consecrated by Agilbert at Compiègne
claims.witness: Stephen 11 (byrhtferth_vita-s-oswaldi-in-historians-of-the-church-of-york-v1-lat_raine1879.txt (Stephen, Life of Wilfrid) l.5207-5220); Bede III.28 (bede_ecclesiastical-history-english-people_giles1903.txt l.8440-8450)

claims.claim: Iona adopted the catholic rites under Abbot Dunchad about eighty years after it sent Aidan
Bede of the departed Irish teachers: their whole care 'was to serve God, not the world — to feed the soul, and not the belly'
The first Easter among the Saxons, and later the change of Easter among the Britons under Elbodug
claims.witness: Annales Cambriae (annales-cambriae-rolls-series-20-lat_williams-ab-ithel1860.txt l.2764, 2984-2986; years 665 and 768 by the editor)

claims.claim: The southern Irish had taken the Roman Easter before Whitby; the northern Irish, Picts, Iona and Welsh changed later
Columbanus trusted the Easter reckoning of his homeland and Anatolius over Victorius

contested_claims.sides: Bede: the practice of Rome and the whole world, Peter, the law and Gospel, Anatolius (bede_ecclesiastical-history-english-people_giles1903.txt l.8002-8192). Stephen: the 318 fathers of Nicaea and the nineteen-year cycle, and the practice of the apostolic see and nearly the whole world (l.5149); it is the king who raises Peter (byrhtferth_vita-s-oswaldi-in-historians-of-the-church-of-york-v1-lat_raine1879.txt (Stephen, Life of Wilfrid) l.5142-5155).

Bede: Oswy questions Colman and Wilfrid, both agree on the keys, and the king rules; then all assent (l.8194-8218). Stephen: Oswy, smiling, asks the whole synod, which answers with one voice; then he rules (l.5152-5200). Both have Oswy rule for Peter.

Bede: she and her followers were for the Scots (l.7966-7967). Stephen: present, with no side (l.5081-5083). Eadmer, twelfth century and dependent, calls her patroness of Colman's party (Raine l.15944-15945). The Mansi heading, held at her request, has no ancient witness (mansi tomus 11 l.7654).
Bede: to consult his people what was to be done (l.8227-8233). Stephen, partisan for Wilfrid: for fear of his own country, leaving his see to a better man (l.5202-5205).
Bede and Stephen call it a synod (Giles l.7958; Raine l.5155). Severinus Binius, in Mansi's note, calls it a collatio, since not all the province's bishops were summoned (mansi tomus 11 l.8053-8058).

claims.claim: Session XV is dated 26 April, ninth indiction; at the Zeuxippus baths a dead man was set on a silver bier; Polychronius laid his statement of faith on him for many hours, whispering, and said he could not raise him; the people cried anathema to the new Simon
The first session met on 7 November, ninth indiction, with the emperor presiding in the hall of the palace called Trullus
The pope's envoys: for forty-six years bishops of Constantinople taught one will and one operation
Agatho: the Roman church has never erred from the path of the apostolic tradition
Macarius and his party: they held what they received from the fathers and from Sergius, Paul, Pyrrhus, Peter, Honorius and Cyrus
Macarius: 'one will and one theandric operation'
Macarius: not even if cut limb from limb and thrown into the sea
The synod cried out to throw out the new Dioscorus, depose him and strip him of his pallium
George of Constantinople accepted Agatho's letters
Session XIII anathematized Honorius 'because of what we found written by him to Sergius'
The definition: 'two natural wills and two natural operations', the human will 'subject to his divine and omnipotent will'
The emperor signed the decrees with his own hand
Counts: 150 (Book of the Popes); 289 (Theophanes); 250 (Michael the Syrian); under 300 with 174 signatures (Percival)
Leo II to the emperor: Honorius tried to overturn the spotless faith by profane betrayal (a margin reading: allowed it to be stained)
Leo II to the bishops of Spain: Honorius fed the flame of heresy by neglect
Agatho died on 10 January 681, by Duchesne's reckoning
Toledo XIV, in the fifth year of Ervig, received the acts so far as they do not depart from earlier councils, and set them after Chalcedon
Michael: Macarius was exiled to Rome and imprisoned to the end of his life; thus came in the pernicious heresy of Maximus
Percival: the Liber Diurnus oath, taken by each new pope from the fifth to the eleventh century, cursed Honorius

contested_claims.sides: Book of the Popes: 150 (l.165717); Paul the Deacon copies it. Theophanes: 289 (l.65259-65261); Eutychius: 289 by his own sum (nicholas-mystikos_epistolae-with-eutychius-alexandrinus-pg111-grc-lat_migne1863.txt l.85490-85551). Michael the Syrian: 250 (l.34486). Percival: under 300, 174 signatures (l.24574-24576). No count of the held list was made.

The acts condemn him (Sessions XIII, XVI, XVIII and the letters). John IV, 641: he meant no contrary wills (denzinger_enchiridion-symbolorum-lat_bannwart1911.txt l.9293-9312). Maximus: the letter meant one human will without contrariety (Mansi note, l.53043-53110). Agatho's letter omits him (l.25303-25306). Leo II: betrayal (l.68856-68866) and neglect (l.102060-102070). Baronius: the name inserted; Percival answers (l.26208-26216).

The acts: he accepted (l.25660-25664). Michael the Syrian: the primates of Constantinople and Antioch refused and were deposed (l.34490-34493). Paul the Deacon: George stirred up the heresy and was rebuked (paul-the-deacon_history-of-the-langobards_foulke1907.txt l.11253-11257, 11283); Foulke calls it a mistake (l.11262-11265).
The acts: 7 November (Mansi l.22004). Book of the Popes: 22 November (l.165715); Duchesne: its dates are nearly all false (l.167013).

contested_claims.claim: Whether the Maronites held to one will after the council
contested_claims.sides: Eutychius calls Macarius a Maronite (nicholas-mystikos_epistolae-with-eutychius-alexandrinus-pg111-grc-lat_migne1863.txt l.84948-84955); William of Tyre: the sixth synod was gathered against them (william-tyre_historia-rerum-in-partibus-transmarinis-gestarum-v2-lat-fra_rhc1844.txt l.26970-26974); Michael the Syrian: under Marwan they confessed one will (michael-the-syrian_chronique-tome2-livres-viii-xi-fra_chabot1901.txt l.39339-39342). Al-Duwayhi: the charge rests on Eutychius (duwayhi_tarikh-al-taifa-al-maruniyya-ara_shartuni189x.txt l.2855-2856). The acts name no Maronites.

contested_claims.claim: The date of Leo II's letter to the emperor
contested_claims.sides: Mirbt: September to December 682 (mirbt_quellen-zur-geschichte-des-papsttums-3e-aufl-deu-lat_1911.txt l.8038). Duchesne: 7 May 683 (l.167074).

claims.claim: The emperor signed first; the next place, 'Locus sanctissimi papae Romani', was left blank; then Paul of Constantinople, Peter of Alexandria, Anastasius of Jerusalem and George of Antioch
The council met in the domed hall of the palace called the Trullus
Hefele dates the council between 1 September 691 and 1 September 692 from the indiction in canon 3
The fifth and sixth councils made no canons; the bishops met at the emperor's command and wrote sacred canons; they ask him to seal them with his signature
Percival counts 211 signers, bishops or representatives of bishops
Basil of Gortyna signed as holding the place of the church of Rome in every synod; whether Rome had sent him there is no information
The Book of the Popes: the envoys of the apostolic see came and, deceived, signed
Percival: the West was not really represented at all
Canon 13 keeps clerical marriages against the Roman rule
Canon 55 forbids the Roman Saturday fast in Lent
Canon 32: in the region of Armenia 'they offer wine only on the Holy Table'; deposition for any bishop or presbyter who will not mix water with it
Canon 36: Constantinople has 'equal privileges with the see of Old Rome', second after it
The canons were sent to Rome in six volumes; Sergius would not receive them or let them be opened and read, and rejected them as invalid
Justinian sent Zacharias to bring the pope to the imperial city; the soldiers of Ravenna and the Pentapolis would not permit it; Zacharias hid under the pope's bed and was driven from Rome
claims.witness: liber-pontificalis_texte-introduction-commentaire-t1-lat-fra_duchesne1886.txt l.170986-170995, 171264-171276; Paul the Deacon VI.11, paul-the-deacon_history-of-the-langobards_foulke1907.txt l.11506-11514

claims.claim: John VII returned the volumes uncorrected, fearful in human weakness
Tarasius at Nicaea II: the same fathers met under Justinian and set forth the canons; 'And let no one doubt concerning them'
In 1054 Niketas cited canon 13 as the sixth synod's; the reply under Humbert's name says the apostolic see never accepted those chapters
Stephen of Taron: the synod of Manazkert required the sacrament without leaven and without water
Ormanian dates the synod of Manazkert to 726
Stephen of Taron's history runs to 1005
Serpos: the Trullan synod was gathered by the Greeks without authority or the pope's consent, a pseudo-synod; its canons rebuke the Armenians without anathematizing the nation
Percival: the bishops were not the same as the Sixth Council's, as the subscriptions show; his note on Tarasius's speech calls it an error

contested_claims.sides: Hefele, in Percival: between 1 September 691 and 1 September 692 (l.26430-26437). Fleury: 692 (l.26385). Duchesne: 692 (LP l.172486). Pedalion: 691 (nikodemos-hagiorite_pedalion-canons-grc_1886.txt l.22318). Theophanes: the second year of Justinian's restored reign (theophanes-confessor_chronographia-pg108-grc-lat_migne1863.txt l.65636-65641); Goar says he errs. Tarasius's 'four or five years' after the Sixth Council (l.39053), which Percival rejects.

Percival, after Hefele: 211 signers (l.26445-26446). Fleury: 211 (l.26387). Balsamon and Zonaras, as the Pedalion reports: 227; the Synodicon: 240 (Pedalion l.22398; Mansi l.98350-98354; the Mansi preface reports 227 as the Greeks' count, l.88684-88685). Mansi's preface: after eight leading signers, the signatures of 205 bishops (mansi tomus 11 l.89062-89081).

Book of the Popes: the envoys signed, deceived (l.170878-170879). Duchesne: they signed and were disowned, their names struck out (l.172488-172497). Percival: the West was not really represented (l.26375-26376). Mansi's preface: no one present in the pope's name (l.88686-88688). Basil of Gortyna signed as holding Rome's place (l.26452-26459). Pedalion: Basil of Gortyna and a bishop of Ravenna held Rome's place (l.22399-22400), against the blank place for Ravenna (Percival l.26451-26452; Mansi l.89074-89075).

The signatures: four, with Anastasius of Jerusalem (Mansi l.95160-95184). The Book of the Popes: three, of Constantinople, Alexandria and Antioch (l.170981-170982). Percival thinks it probable they were present.

contested_claims.claim: Whether later popes accepted the canons
contested_claims.sides: Book of the Popes: John VII returned them uncorrected; Constantine's life does not name them. Percival: a middle course under Constantine (l.26466-26468). Foulke, after Hodgkin: probably accepted (paul-the-deacon_history-of-the-langobards_foulke1907.txt l.12156-12157). Duchesne: the John VII episode is otherwise unknown (l.175180-175188).

contested_claims.claim: Whether the bishops were those of the Sixth Council
contested_claims.sides: Tarasius, 787: the same (l.39053-39058). Percival: not the same (l.26420-26422). Mansi's preface: only forty-three the same (l.89082-89085).

claims.claim: In the Holy Apostles, the bishops began to read the Scriptures while the rulers watched; the guards burst in with drawn swords threatening to kill the patriarch and bishops; bishops of their mind went out shouting 'Vicimus'; the synod was dissolved
The Hieria council had 338 bishops
The Hieria decree, in Percival's summary mostly from Hefele: the image of Christ either depicts the Godhead or separates the body; the only admissible figure is bread and wine
Tarasius demanded an ecumenical council with legates from Rome and the East, since the Christians of the East decline communion
The council met by the will of Constantine and Irene, at Nicaea in the church named Sophia
The Book of the Popes: about 350 bishops; the acts translated into Latin and kept in the library
Michael the Monk: about 350 fathers, Plato among them
Theophanes: first session at Holy Wisdom, Nicaea, on 11 October; in November the decree read at the Magnaura and signed by the emperor and his mother
Duchesne: eight sessions from 25 September to 22 October 787
Session I: penitent bishops received; Tarasius on calumniators become advocates
Session IV: 'Shall we not weep when we see an image of our crucified Lord?'
The decree: images given honourable reverence, not latria; the honour passes to the prototype
Duchesne: the Latin translation shocked the Frankish clergy and moved Charlemagne to fight the council
Frankfurt 794 rejected the Greek synod as anathematizing those who would not give images service or adoration as to the Trinity
Hefele: the Franks misjudged through false translation and misunderstanding
Constantine of Constantia reserved the worship of adoration to the Trinity
Paris 825: Charlemagne's chapters sent by Angilbert; Hadrian answered; Nicaea had erred
In 843 the council gained firm authority
Photius: at its sessions the iconoclasts were defeated
After Irene's death in 803 several iconoclast rulers held the throne

contested_claims.claim: The day of the broken meeting at the Holy Apostles
contested_claims.sides: Goar's Latin of Theophanes: 17 August, ninth indiction (l.83399-83400). Anastasius's Latin: 7 August (l.123640).

Theophanes: first session 11 October (l.123692-123695). Duchesne: eight sessions, 25 September to 22 October (LP l.207927-207928). No held act gives a session date. Editor's note in Migne PG 99: begun 8 Kalends October (24 September), indiction 11, 787 (theodore-studite_opera-omnia-pg99-grc-lat_migne1860.txt l.69540-69541). W. M. Sinclair, quoted by Percival: seven sittings (npnf214 l.39596-39597).

contested_claims.claim: Whether the Eastern envoys were sent by their patriarchs
contested_claims.sides: The acts: they brought letters from the East (l.38527-38531). Theodore the Studite, 826, as Percival quotes him from Neale: brought by our deputies, not sent (l.41526-41536); he later changed his view.

contested_claims.claim: Whether the Franks misread the council
contested_claims.sides: Frankfurt c.2 (CAP l.5607-5609). Hefele via Percival: false translation (l.38983-38992). Boretius, citing Hefele: 'non recte iudicavit' (CAP l.5680-5682); one witness, not two. Duchesne (LP l.207933-207935). Paris 825 still rejects adoration (M14 l.45079-45080).
Percival inclines to Alcuin (l.41658-41664); Froben denies it (alcuin_opera-omnia-letters_migne-pl100-101_1863.txt l.92603-92760). Not held.

claims.claim: Eighth session, the Nones of November, Basil's third year, third indiction, Basil presiding

At Basil's command the pledges Photius took from great and small, down to leather-workers, fishmongers, wood-sellers and needle-makers, with the books against Nicholas and the acts against Ignatius, were cast into the fire
The Greek text of 861 is lost
Hadrian II ordered every copy of 867's acts burned; copies burned at Rome and by the council
Photius was made patriarch from a layman in six days
Nicholas sent Radoald and Zacharias only to inquire
Seventy-two perjured witnesses; Ignatius stripped; Procopius cried 'Indignus' and Zacharias and Radoald with him
Nicholas's Roman synod deposed Zacharias and condemned Radoald
Boris was baptized and asked for clergy from Louis and Nicholas
Photius's encyclical: the Latins fell on Bulgaria like a wild boar on the Lord's vineyard; they taught the Spirit proceeds from the Son also
Photius's council of 867 condemned and anathematized Nicholas
Anastasius: about a thousand forged signatures, only twenty-one bishops agreeing
Basil put Photius out
Hadrian asked for a numerous council with his envoys presiding
Canon 4: Photius never was nor is a bishop
Nicetas: 102 bishops
Three days after the last session the Eastern vicars assigned Bulgaria to Constantinople over the Roman envoys' protest
John VIII asked that the synod held against Photius in Hadrian's time be null and void
Photius presided at the second session of 879, with the Roman envoys
The definition of 879-880: nothing taken away, nothing added, nothing changed, nothing corrupted
The Pedalion: 383 fathers at 879; the council called eighth by the Latins, the one against Photius, was rejected by the one for Photius

Mark of Ephesus at Florence: the council of 879, also called the eighth, rescinded the acts against Photius; in the great church of Constantinople an anathema is read on all written or said against the holy patriarchs Photius and Ignatius
Will: Photius died in 891
Basil put Photius out and restored Ignatius to the patriarch's palace

claims.claim: The seventeen canons of the synod of 861 in the Holy Apostles
The Pedalion's editors: the synod of 861 met in 861, issued its canons at its second meeting, its minutes are not found, and it said nothing against Photius

contested_claims.sides: Binius: 318, 'ut ipsi jactabant', as they boasted (mansi_sacrorum-conciliorum-collectio-tomus-15-lat_welter-facsimile1902.txt l.63831, 63849-63850). Pedalion: 318, after Dositheos (nikodemos-hagiorite_pedalion-canons-grc_1886.txt l.33224). Nicholas I: the Byzantines claimed nearly Nicaea's number (mansi_sacrorum-conciliorum-collectio-tomus-15-lat_welter-facsimile1902.txt l.18456-18458).
Acts, ninth session: more than a hundred (M16 l.36866-36892). Nicetas: 102 (l.26091-26092); the Greek tract: 102 (l.41349-41351). Binius: 101 signers (l.48269-48288). Not counted for this profile.
Pedalion: 383 (l.34522); Binius after Baronius: 383 (M17 l.38451-38452). Nilus: 380 (l.38862-38866). Greek tract: 380, doubting it (M16 l.43262-43282).

contested_claims.claim: Which council is the eighth ecumenical
contested_claims.sides: Latins: 869-870 (Pedalion l.14346-14348; Will l.16709-16714). Nilus: 879 (M17 l.38862). Mark of Ephesus: 879 (M31 l.53653-53656). Pedalion: both only improperly ecumenical (l.14340-14348). Leo IX: seven councils (Will l.16687-16690).

contested_claims.claim: Whether the sixth and seventh sessions of 879-880 are genuine
contested_claims.sides: Unsigned note in Mansi: forged by Photius (M17 l.52604-52628). Nilus reports the definition (l.38880-38895).

contested_claims.claim: Whether John VIII later anathematized Photius
contested_claims.sides: Binius after Baronius, and Formosus's letter as Binius quotes it (M17 l.38375-38425); Will (l.3980-3987). No letter of John's own held.

contested_claims.claim: The month of the council of 861
contested_claims.sides: Pagi, reckoning from Nicetas's Pentecost (25 May 861) and the Libellus synodicus, 'post Pascha anni Chr. 861' (M15 l.63995-64010).
The Book of the Popes: to inquire into Ignatius's removal (l.49600-49604); also on images (l.48974-48975). The Pedalion: against the iconoclasts (l.33227-33228).
